Court.title: Court
Court.description: Represents a judicial court or tribunal within the legal system, including Supreme, High, and District courts.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Court entity.

name.description: The official name of the court (e.g., Supreme Court, Allahabad High Court).

type.description: The type or level of the court (e.g., Supreme, High, District, Tribunal).

jurisdictionRegion.description: The geographical or administrative region over which the court has jurisdiction (e.g., Delhi NCT, Uttar Pradesh). Used for regional grouping in dashboards.

location.description: The physical location of the court (e.g., New Delhi, Prayagraj).

totalPendingCases.description: The current total number of pending cases in this court.

newCasesThisYear.description: The number of new cases registered in this court during the current year.

disposedCasesThisYear.description: The number of cases disposed of by this court during the current year.

disposalRatePercentage.description: The calculated percentage of cases disposed relative to total or new cases, representing efficiency.

sanctionedJudgePosts.description: The total number of approved judge positions for this court.

occupiedJudgePosts.description: The number of judge positions currently filled in this court.

vacantJudgePosts.description: The number of judge positions currently vacant in this court.

averageWaitingTimeYears.description: The average waiting period for case resolution in this court, measured in years.

statusIndicator.description: A symbolic indicator (e.g., 🟢, 🟡, 🔴) representing the overall performance or health status of the court, derived from various metrics.

createdAt.description: Timestamp when this court record was created.

updatedAt.description: Timestamp when this court record was last updated.

Judge.title: Judge
Judge.description: Represents a judge within the judicial system, including their profile and performance metrics.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Judge entity.

firstName.description: The first name of the judge.

lastName.description: The last name of the judge.

fullName.description: The full name of the judge, derived from first and last names.

email.description: The email address of the judge, used for contact or profile management.

courtId.description: Reference to the Court where this judge is currently serving. (Relationship: Court 1:N Judge)

appointmentDate.description: The date when the judge was appointed.

retirementDate.description: The date when the judge is expected to retire or has retired (optional).

currentCasesAssigned.description: The number of cases currently assigned to this judge for hearing or resolution.

casesDisposedThisYear.description: The number of cases disposed of by this judge in the current year.

totalCasesDisposed.description: The total number of cases disposed of by this judge throughout their career.

seniorityRank.description: The seniority rank of the judge within their court or the overall judicial system.

status.description: The current status of the judge (e.g., Active, On Leave, Retired).

createdAt.description: Timestamp when this judge's record was created.

updatedAt.description: Timestamp when this judge's record was last updated.

Case.title: Case
Case.description: Represents a legal case being processed in a court, tracking its status and assignment.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Case entity.

caseNumber.description: The unique identifying number for the legal case.

title.description: A brief title or subject of the case.

description.description: A detailed description or summary of the case.

status.description: The current status of the case (e.g., Filed, Hearing Scheduled, In Progress, Disposed, Appealed).

filingDate.description: The date and time when the case was officially filed.

lastHearingDate.description: The date and time of the last hearing for this case (optional).

nextHearingDate.description: The date and time of the next scheduled hearing for this case (optional).

disposalDate.description: The date and time when the case was officially disposed of (if applicable).

courtId.description: Reference to the Court where this case is being heard. (Relationship: Court 1:N Case)

judgeId.description: Reference to the Judge currently assigned to this case. (Relationship: Judge 1:N Case)

caseTypeId.description: Reference to the CaseType that categorizes this case. (Relationship: CaseType 1:N Case)

isVideoConferenceCase.description: Indicates whether the case proceedings involve video conferencing, part of e-Court integration.

createdAt.description: Timestamp when this case record was created.

updatedAt.description: Timestamp when this case record was last updated.

CaseType.title: CaseType
CaseType.description: Defines different categories or types of legal cases.

id.description: Unique identifier for the CaseType entity.

name.description: The name of the case type (e.g., 'दीवानी मामले' (Civil Cases), 'आपराधिक मामले' (Criminal Cases)).

description.description: A detailed description explaining what this case type encompasses.

createdAt.description: Timestamp when this case type record was created.

updatedAt.description: Timestamp when this case type record was last updated.

Alert.title: Alert
Alert.description: Represents a system-generated alert or notification regarding significant judicial events, statistics, or critical issues.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Alert entity.

message.description: The content or textual description of the alert.

type.description: The classification of the alert (e.g., Critical, Warning, Info, Update).

severity.description: A numerical value indicating the severity level of the alert (e.g., 1 for Critical, 2 for Warning, 3 for Info).

generatedDate.description: The date and time when the alert was generated.

associatedCourtId.description: Optional reference to the Court entity if the alert is specific to a particular court. (Relationship: Court 0..1:N Alert)

associatedJudgeId.description: Optional reference to the Judge entity if the alert is specific to a particular judge. (Relationship: Judge 0..1:N Alert)

isRead.description: Indicates whether the alert has been marked as read by a user.

isDismissed.description: Indicates whether the alert has been dismissed by a user.

createdAt.description: Timestamp when this alert record was created.

updatedAt.description: Timestamp when this alert record was last updated.

CourtMetricSnapshot.title: CourtMetricSnapshot
CourtMetricSnapshot.description: Captures historical statistical data for a court at a specific point in time, used for trend analysis and historical comparisons.

id.description: Unique identifier for the CourtMetricSnapshot entity.

courtId.description: Reference to the Court for which this snapshot data is recorded. (Relationship: Court 1:N CourtMetricSnapshot)

snapshotDate.description: The date and time when this metric snapshot was taken (e.g., end of month or year).

totalPendingCasesCount.description: The total number of pending cases in the court at the time of this snapshot.

cumulativeNewCases.description: The cumulative total of new cases registered in the court up to the snapshot date.

cumulativeDisposedCases.description: The cumulative total of cases disposed of by the court up to the snapshot date.

vacantJudgePostsCount.description: The number of vacant judge posts in the court at the time of this snapshot.

averageWaitingTimeYears.description: The average waiting time for case resolution in the court at the time of this snapshot, in years.

createdAt.description: Timestamp when this snapshot record was created.

updatedAt.description: Timestamp when this snapshot record was last updated.

AdminSetting.title: AdminSetting
AdminSetting.description: Stores various configuration settings managed by administrators, such as performance targets or application defaults.

id.description: Unique identifier for the AdminSetting entity.

settingName.description: A unique name for the administrative setting (e.g., 'MonthlyDisposalTarget', 'DefaultAverageWaitingTime').

settingValue.description: The value of the setting, stored as a string to accommodate various data types (numbers, booleans, JSON objects).

description.description: A clear explanation of what this setting controls or affects.

associatedCourtId.description: Optional reference to the Court entity if the setting is specific to a particular court. (Relationship: Court 0..1:N AdminSetting)

associatedJudgeId.description: Optional reference to the Judge entity if the setting is specific to a particular judge. (Relationship: Judge 0..1:N AdminSetting)

isActive.description: Indicates whether this administrative setting is currently active and in use.

lastUpdatedByUserId.description: Reference to the ID of the user who last updated this setting (assuming an external User entity).

createdAt.description: Timestamp when this setting record was created.

updatedAt.description: Timestamp when this setting record was last updated.

params.name: userId

firestore.reasoning:
The Firestore structure for the 'न्यायदृष्टि' dashboard is designed with a strong emphasis on Authorization Independence, Structural Segregation, and clear Access Modeling to ensure security, scalability, and debuggability. All entities are generally stored in top-level collections to avoid deep, restrictive hierarchies and facilitate flexible querying. This approach enables robust `list` operations (QAPs) without requiring complex rule filters.

**Authorization Independence (Strategy A):**
*   **Top-Level Collections:** Collections like `/courts`, `/judges`, `/cases`, `/caseTypes`, `/alerts`, and `/adminSettings` are top-level. This means that access rules for a document in these collections do not depend on data from a parent document (e.g., accessing a `Judge` document does not require reading its `Court` parent). Instead, necessary foreign keys (`courtId`, `judgeId`) are denormalized directly into the respective documents. For example, a `Judge` document contains `courtId`, and a `Case` document contains `courtId` and `judgeId`. This allows rules to evaluate authorization solely based on the document being accessed and the `request.auth.uid`, eliminating expensive and complex `get()` calls in security rules. Atomic operations across related entities (e.g., creating a new case and updating court metrics) are also simplified.
*   **Subcollection for Snapshots:** The `CourtMetricSnapshot` entity is a subcollection of `Court` (`/courts/{courtId}/metricSnapshots/{snapshotId}`). This hierarchy is chosen because snapshots are intrinsically historical data *for* a specific court. Authorization for a snapshot implicitly depends on access to its parent court. However, since courts themselves are generally readable by authenticated users (and mutable by admins), the `courtId` being part of the path (and present in the document) is sufficient. Rules do not need to `get()` the parent `Court` document to determine if a user can access its snapshots, as the court's existence and the user's general authorization level (e.g., authenticated user, admin) are typically checked at the collection level.

**QAPs (Rules are not Filters):**
*   **Homogeneous Security Posture (Strategy B):** Each collection (`/courts`, `/judges`, `/cases`, etc.) is designed to hold documents with a similar security posture. For example, all `Court` documents are broadly visible to authenticated users, and all `AdminSetting` documents are exclusively for administrators. This structural segregation simplifies security rules significantly. Instead of rules filtering out unauthorized documents from a broad collection, the structure itself defines what can be listed.
*   **DBAC (Strategy C.4):** A dedicated `roles_admin/{userId}` collection implements Database Access Control. The *existence* of a document in this collection (`exists(/databases/$(database)/documents/roles_admin/$(request.auth.uid))`) is used to grant administrative privileges. This avoids custom claims and makes rules explicit and debuggable.
*   **Path-Based & Denormalized Access (Strategy C.1, C.2, C.3):** For entities like `Judge` and `Case`, their association with `Court` is maintained through `courtId` (and `judgeId`) fields directly within their documents. This allows efficient queries and secure `list` operations (e.g., `db.collection('cases').where('courtId', '==', 'court123')`) where the results are pre-filtered by the query, and rules simply confirm the user's general read access to cases, rather than filtering results *after* they've been retrieved.

In summary, the design prioritizes flat, top-level collections where possible, with necessary authorization contexts denormalized into the documents themselves. Subcollections are used only when there's a strong logical and authorization-transparent parent-child relationship. A dedicated role collection manages administrative access, ensuring clear and auditable security rules.
